data.name: Munar
data.gender_notes: Munar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Al-Munir' which means 'The One Who Illuminates'. This name is associated with the moon and the night. The name Munar carries the meaning “Moon” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Munar usually hope their child will grow to embody moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: This name is believed to be associated with the divine and the supernatural, as the moon is often considered a symbol of the divine in Islamic culture.
data.etymology: Munar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Munar total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

His book, Munjid al-Buldan (Guide to the Countries), is a comprehensive geographical and historical description of the Islamic world during his time. In this work, he mentions a town named Munar, which was located in the Maghreb region, near the Mediterranean coast.

historical_references.context: Al-Idrisi was a geographer and traveller from Sicily. His book, Nuzhat al-Mushtaq fi Ikhtiraq al-Afaq (The Pleasurable Journey in Search of Knowledge), is a detailed description of the Islamic world, including its geography, cities, and provinces. It mentions a town named Munar, which was located in the Fez province of Morocco.
